Landing.title: quickdraw
Landing.tagline: The realtime fullstack starter for quickdraw-core
Landing.subtitle: Typed Socket.IO services, two-tier access control, a full auth suite, and a multiplayer game foundation — already wired together. Fork it and build the interesting part.
Landing.featRealtimeDesc: Request/response methods, live subscriptions, and fire-and-forget channels over Socket.IO — end-to-end typed, zod-validated, cached with TanStack Query.
Landing.featRealtimeDetail: One defineMethod call gives you a validated, ACL-gated, acknowledged Socket.IO endpoint — and the client consumes it through a typed hook with caching and auto-invalidation. No REST boilerplate, no drift between client and server types.
Landing.featAclDesc: Service-level roles plus per-entry ACLs (JSON or membership tables), enforced server-side on every method, subscription, and channel.
Landing.featAclDetail: Core checks service-level roles first (Public/Read/Moderate/Admin from user.serviceAccess), then hands per-entry decisions to your service. ChatService overrides checkEntryACL with a membership table; DocumentService uses the built-in JSON ACL — both patterns ship working.
Landing.featGameDesc: A Godot 4 snake demo with real netcode: 20Hz input channels, client prediction, snapshot interpolation, server-side NPCs, and React overlays driving the sim.
Landing.featGameDetail: Channels are the high-frequency counterpart to methods: fire-and-forget, zod-validated per message, rate-limited by a per-socket token bucket, and gated on room membership. The Godot client speaks the same wire format through a first-party GDScript Socket.IO client — game commands stay ordinary quickdraw methods a React button can call too.
Landing.featAuthDesc: Google & Discord OAuth, revocable sessions, guest play, a Discord Activity embed — and a mock OAuth flow so local dev never needs real credentials.
Landing.featAuthDetail: Sessions are JWTs paired with revocable database rows, carried only in an httpOnly cookie — the same credential authenticates REST and every socket. Guest sessions mint real (marked) users so anonymous players get scores and chat; the mock OAuth provider runs a genuine code flow against seeded users and hard-blocks production boot.
Landing.featAdminDesc: Every service gets an admin CRUD surface for free — the game's live-tunable variables are edited right in the browser.
Landing.featAdminDetail: installAdminMethods exposes list/get/create/update/delete with per-action access levels, and the generic /admin UI renders tables and editors from the schema — no per-service admin pages to build. The game's tunables (definitions) are edited live this way.
Landing.featTestingDesc: Integration tests run on in-memory PGlite locally (seconds, no setup) and real PostgreSQL in CI — the same suite, both places.
Landing.featTestingDetail: startTestServer boots the full Socket.IO server on an ephemeral port; connectAsUser and emitWithAck drive it like a real client. TEST_DATABASE_URL flips the database between fingerprint-cached in-memory PGlite (local default) and per-worker cloned PostgreSQL (CI).
Landing.featDeployDesc: GitHub Actions for drift checks, lint, types, and sharded tests, plus a one-click deploy pipeline to Cloud Run and Vercel.
Landing.featDeployDetail: CI fails PRs on migration drift and runs cached lint/typecheck/build plus sharded integration tests against real PostgreSQL. The deploy workflow chains a secret scan, Prisma migrations, a Docker image to Cloud Run, and the web app to Vercel — fill in the placeholders and it's one click.
Landing.featGuardrailsDesc: Strict lint rules ship with the framework and update with it, a custom-rule showcase is one file away, and path-scoped Claude rules keep agents on the rails.
Landing.featGuardrailsDetail: The oxlint config extends quickdraw-core's shipped base (strict categories, the quickdraw rule plugin, complexity budgets) so best practices update with the package. eslint-plugin-project shows how to add your own rules — no-prisma-in-routes ships as the example — and .claude/rules/*.md load automatically when Claude Code touches matching paths.
Landing.featForkDesc: init-fork.sh renames the whole identity — app, database, deploy targets — and can carve out the game foundation cleanly if you don't need it.
Landing.featForkDetail: One script rewrites databases, display names, deploy service names, the devcontainer, and optionally the backend port and package scope — then deletes itself. --without-game removes the entire game foundation along marked seams and verifies the result builds before it finishes.
